input.reason: I read src/api.ts and its only caller, src/dashboard.ts. `fetchCurrentUser` returns `json<User>(res)`, and `json` throws whenever `!res.ok`. `loadDashboard` awaits it at line 27 without a try/catch. `mountDashboard` calls `void loadDashboard(...)`, so the rejection is dropped and the render callback never runs. F01 holds as written. F03 is partly wrong: `fetchUserList` wraps its whole body in try/catch and returns `[]` on a non-ok status or any thrown error, so a failed user-list request cannot reject the dashboard load. F03 is edited so it only blames `fetchCurrentUser`. The repo has no tests, no unhandledrejection handler and no other caller that would catch the error.
input.summary: fetchCurrentUser errors reject loadDashboard uncaught; dashboard never renders

findings.text: `fetchCurrentUser` rejects on any non-2xx status, and `loadDashboard` does not catch it.
findings.reason: Claim 1: `fetchCurrentUser` rejects on any non-2xx status. It returns `json<User>(res)` (api.ts:13), and `json` runs `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)` (api.ts:7). `res.ok` is false for every status outside 200–299. Claim 2: `loadDashboard` does not catch it. api.ts:27 is `const me = await fetchCurrentUser();` with no try/catch, and the only caller, dashboard.ts:5, calls `void loadDashboard(...)` with no `.catch`.

findings.text: `loadDashboard` awaits `fetchCurrentUser` with no error handling. A failed request from `fetchCurrentUser` rejects the dashboard load, and the page never renders.
findings.reason: The central claim holds for `fetchCurrentUser`: it throws on a non-ok response (api.ts:7), and `loadDashboard` awaits it at line 27 without a try/catch. The rejection stops `render` from being called, and dashboard.ts discards the promise with `void`, so the root keeps showing "Loading...". The claim does not hold for `fetchUserList`. Its whole body is inside try/catch, and it returns `[]` on a non-ok status or any thrown error, so a failed user-list request cannot reject the dashboard load. The "either one" wording and the mention of `fetchUserList` as unhandled were removed.

input.severity_reason: This only happens when the `/api/me` request fails, from a non-2xx response or a network error. That is an error path, not normal use. When it happens, the dashboard stays on "Loading..." with no error shown and an unhandled promise rejection. No data is lost and there is no security impact.
